msg: architecture/decisions.md SIM-7: ZVS at every bus point. 30 V is the owner's bench point and the voltage the recommended populate is tuned at.
SIM-7 at the bottom of the owner's 25-30 V bench range. This is the WORST bus point for ZVS, not the best - see zvs_drift_25_40_v.
SIM-7 at the H4-ruled 36 V / 162 W derated bus.
SIM-7 at the original 40 V design bus.

QUANTIFIES decisions.md D1's central claim that 'the bus can be backed down at bring-up WITHOUT LOSING ZVS'. Exactly true only for a LINEAR shunt; here more than 70 percent of C_shunt is EPC2019 Coss(v), whose charge-equivalent RISES as the swing shrinks, so a lower bus is a larger effective shunt and ZVS arrives LATE. 6 V is one full ZVS window: inside it the derating ladder is usable, outside it D1's ladder is void.
architecture/decisions.md SIM-7 window: 162 W at the H4-ruled 36 V bus.
112.6 W at the owner's 30 V bench point (0.51663.Vdd^2/R at R_opt 4.13).
decisions.md OPEN-4 brackets the 40 V output at 200-223 W because the two Sokal power coefficients disagree; this window covers the bracket.

architecture SIM-1's 1.29x derate on the EPC2019's 200 V BVDSS. A populate trimmed at 30 V is UNDER-shunted at 40 V (the nonlinear Coss supplies less charge-equivalent capacitance over a larger swing), which raises the drain peak. If this fails, one populate cannot serve both bus points and 40 V needs its own bank setting.
Same derate at the bottom of the bench range.

Vds,pk/Vdd. Exactly linear Class E holds this constant at ~3.56 (decisions.md D9's 142.5 V at 40 V). The spread across 25-40 V is the same nonlinear-Coss effect as zvs_drift, expressed as stress instead of timing.
Vds,pk/Vdd at 25 V, for the ratio against vdspk_per_vdd_40.
P(40 V)/P(30 V). Exact Vdd^2 linearity gives (40/30)^2 = 1.778; the measured departure is the quantitative size of D1's linearity assumption.
